text_input: Patient was apparently normal 4 days back when she got up from bed and went to the washroom, where she noticed angle of mouth deviation to the right side. This was followed by slurring of speech. The patient was able to understand what the attendees were saying (telling).Patient is an Anganwadi worker and continued to go to work for the past 4 days, ignoring her current symptoms.Patient complained of giddiness (1 episode) shortly after getting up from bed. The episode was not associated with tinnitus or Loss of Consciousness. Patient sat down on the floor for support and rested for some time. She was taken to St. Martha’s Hospital, during which time she noticed paucity (weakness/reduced movement) of left upper and lower limbs. This was accompanied by a "dragging type of pain." Despite this, the patient was still able to walk by herself. MRI Brain done in which showed a Right (R) MCA territory infarct with a Right (R) MCA cutoff (indicating a blockage in the Middle Cerebral Artery). Patient was advised admission at St. Martha’s, but went home due to financial issues. Yesterday morning, the patient was taken to NIMHANS.Due to the non-availability of beds at NIMHANS, she was referred to KIMS. No h/o Swaying while walking/ Smell disturbance / Diplopia (double vision) / Blurring of vision/ Difficulty in chewing / swallowing (Dysphagia)/Tinnitus / Hearing loss/ Vomiting / Headache / Neck pain/ Nasal intonation / Nasal regurgitation/ Involuntary movements of body/ Tingling sensation / Numbness / Loss of sensation/ Bowel / Bladder disturbances/Fever.
